source: Guo et al. (2024) DS-Agent: Automated Data Science by Empowering LLMs with Case-Based Reasoning
finding: Case = task description plus solution (insight text or script). Human cases are Kaggle winner reports and top code summarised to text. Agent cases are task plus the Python script that worked. Cases are retained only when test performance improved.
numbers: Development stage: GPT-4 success rate 100% on 12 tasks (5 trials). Deployment: one-pass rate 99% (GPT-4) and 85% (GPT-3.5) over 18 tasks; best baseline 60% and 56%.
limits: Kaggle data science only. Compared against ResearchAgent, AutoGPT-style baselines. Authors' own benchmark.
agent_relevance: Store the problem plus a working solution, and write a case only when the outcome beat the prior best.

source: Guo et al. (2024) DS-Agent: Automated Data Science by Empowering LLMs with Case-Based Reasoning
finding: Ablation of case type: reusing past agent cases (task plus working code, homogeneous) beat reusing textual human insights (heterogeneous) in nearly all deployment tasks.
numbers: Figure 6a: agent-case variant above the human-insight-text variant on nearly all 18 tasks (exact bars not in text).
limits: Single paper. Exact per-task numbers only in a figure.
agent_relevance: A case that keeps the concrete problem and solution together beats a free-text lesson alone.

source: Guo et al. (2024) DS-Agent: Automated Data Science by Empowering LLMs with Case-Based Reasoning
finding: Number of retrieved cases in context: zero cases is worst, but more cases made performance fall quickly. Fewer was better.
numbers: Zero retrieved cases = zero-shot level (worst). Performance declined rapidly as cases rose (text: 'rapid decline', unexpected for few-shot).
limits: Exact curve is in Figure 6b. Code-generation task only.
agent_relevance: Retrieve few cases. One or two. More cases hurt.

source: Guo et al. (2024) DS-Agent: Automated Data Science by Empowering LLMs with Case-Based Reasoning
finding: ReviseRank: letting the LLM re-rank retrieved cases using the last execution feedback beat taking the top embedding match. Removing CBR entirely gave the worst variant.
numbers: Ablation (Table 2, avg best rank over 12 dev tasks, 5 trials): w/o CBR worst, w/o ReviseRank in between, full best (numbers in table, not extracted in text).
limits: Rank gaps in table; not significance-tested.
agent_relevance: Case utility depends on the current failure, not only on problem similarity. Re-rank by the latest outcome.

source: Guo et al. (2024) DS-Agent: Automated Data Science by Empowering LLMs with Case-Based Reasoning
finding: Authors discuss an echo chamber risk: cases made by the LLM can amplify its own bias. Their defence is a quality filter (keep only high-performing solutions) and human cases from the leaderboard.
numbers: No measured test of the echo-chamber risk.
limits: Argued, not measured.
agent_relevance: Only retain outcome-verified cases; keep some externally sourced cases.

source: Wiratunga et al. (2024) CBR-RAG: Case-Based Reasoning for Retrieval Augmented Generation in LLMs for Legal Question Answering
finding: Case is a tuple of Q (question), A (answer), S (support text), E (entities from S). Each case gets two embeddings: intra (question to question similarity) and inter (question to support or entity relevance). Hybrid weighted retrieval mixes them.
numbers: Casebase 2,084 legal Q-A-support cases (2,124 minus 40). 32 test questions built from pairs of parent cases. Best retrieval: hybrid AnglEBERT weights [0.25,0.40,0.35], k=3.
limits: Test set only 32 items; generated by Mistral-7B. Metric is cosine similarity to a reference answer, not a human judge. No domain expert review.
agent_relevance: Case design choice: store the evidence (support) in the case, not only problem and answer.

source: Wiratunga et al. (2024) CBR-RAG: Case-Based Reasoning for Retrieval Augmented Generation in LLMs for Legal Question Answering
finding: Giving full cases (Q, A, S, E) in the prompt beat support text alone in most hybrid variants. Best setup beat the no-retrieval baseline by 1.94% in answer similarity.
numbers: Best cosine similarity 0.9141 (hybrid AnglEBERT, k=3, full case) against about 0.8967 for No-RAG. One-tailed t-test p<0.05 vs No-RAG and vs hybrid LegalBERT k=3; only 90% level vs hybrid BERT k=1.
limits: Small gain, small test set, high baseline because the model already knows law. General embedding (AnglEBERT, contrastive) beat the legal-domain LegalBERT.
agent_relevance: Showing the whole case record helps more than showing just the lesson text. The gain is small when the model already knows the domain.

source: Hu et al. (2024) Case-Based or Rule-Based: How Do Transformers Do the Math? (ICML 2024)
finding: Models learn math by case matching, not rules. In a leave-square-out test, accuracy fails inside the held-out region and is worse the farther from the training cases. Same with a scratchpad.
numbers: Random split: 100% accuracy on all datasets. Leave-Square-Out (training set above 95% of data): accuracy drops, and drops further as test-square side grows (10, 20, 30, 40 on GPT-2 and GPT-2-medium).
limits: Small fine-tuned models on five arithmetic-style tasks. Not a test of prompted frontier models.
agent_relevance: LLM reasoning is partly nearest-case matching. Cases near the problem help; far cases do not. Rules in the prompt can fix this.

source: Hu et al. (2024) Case-Based or Rule-Based: How Do Transformers Do the Math? (ICML 2024)
finding: Rule-Following Fine-Tuning: put explicit rules in the input and have the model recite and follow them step by step. This generalised addition to longer digit lengths where direct and scratchpad training failed.
numbers: Llama-2-7B with RFFT generalised to 6 to 9 digit addition (exact accuracy in Figure 7, not extracted).
limits: Fine-tuning, not scaffolding. Arithmetic only.
agent_relevance: Where an exact rule exists, store and apply the rule (a case-to-rule step) instead of more cases.

source: Zhao et al. (2024) ExpeL: LLM Agents Are Experiential Learners (AAAI)
finding: Two memory forms are used together: (1) a vector store of successful trajectories retrieved by task similarity, (2) a list of natural-language insights extracted from success and failure pairs. Neither alone is best everywhere.
numbers: Insights-only vs retrieval-only: HotpotQA 36% vs 31%; ALFWorld 50% vs 55%. Full ExpeL beat ReAct on HotpotQA, ALFWorld, WebShop (gpt-3.5-turbo-0613 actor).
limits: Averages with std errors; small benchmarks. Insights help knowledge tasks, trajectories help action tasks.
agent_relevance: Our S9 record should hold both a concrete example and a short lesson line.

source: Zhao et al. (2024) ExpeL: LLM Agents Are Experiential Learners (AAAI)
finding: Ablations on retrieval and extraction. Random trajectories hurt; task-similar ones helped most. Adding reflections into insight extraction hurt. Hand-written insights were weaker than LLM-written ones.
numbers: ALFWorld: ReAct 40.0%, reasoning-similarity retrieval 48.5%, random 42.5%, ExpeL task-similarity 59.0%. HotpotQA: ReAct 28.0%, ExpeL 39.0%; hand-crafted insights and reflection-augmented insights both scored below ExpeL (32.0 and 29.0 as listed in Table 3).
limits: Table values read from extracted text; column labels may be shifted. One model family.
agent_relevance: Retrieval key matters: index by the task description, not by the latest step.

source: Zhao et al. (2024) ExpeL: LLM Agents Are Experiential Learners (AAAI)
finding: Insight extraction needs real experience including failures. Extracting insights from only the few-shot examples gave no gain over ReAct. Cases from Reflexion-style retries (success and failure pairs) beat cases from a no-retry run.
numbers: HotpotQA ablation (Figure 6): few-shot-only insights about equal to ReAct; ReAct-gathered experience better; Reflexion-gathered best.
limits: Figure only; no exact numbers in text.
agent_relevance: Failure-then-success pairs are the richest source of lessons. Store the pair.

source: Zhao et al. (2024) ExpeL: LLM Agents Are Experiential Learners (AAAI)
finding: Cross-task transfer: insights learned on HotpotQA transferred to FEVER with a small amount of fine-tuning examples. ExpeL matched Reflexion without retries on test tasks.
numbers: FEVER success: Act 58%, ReAct 63%, ExpeL without task demos 65%, ExpeL 70%. ALFWorld: ReAct+Reflexion R0 40.3% to R3 54.4%; ExpeL retrieve-only 54.5% at R0; ExpeL+Reflexion 59.0% to 64.2%.
limits: One source-target pair. Same backbone throughout.
agent_relevance: Lessons written as general text move across task types; raw trajectories do not.

source: Wang et al. (2024) Agent Workflow Memory
finding: Stored unit is a workflow: a reusable sub-routine induced from trajectories, with example-specific values replaced by placeholders. Works offline from training data or online from the agent's own judged-successful runs.
numbers: Relative gains of 24.6% on Mind2Web and 51.1% on WebArena (23.5% to 35.5% success, GPT-4); about 2 fewer steps per task. Online AWM beat baselines by 8.9 to 14.0 absolute points as train-test gap grew.
limits: Web navigation only. Online mode relies on an LLM judge for success labels.
agent_relevance: Abstracted routines transfer better than whole traces.

source: Wang et al. (2024) Agent Workflow Memory
finding: Abstract workflows beat concrete example retrieval (Synapse) on Mind2Web cross-task. The authors say full examples bias the agent toward example-specific elements.
numbers: Against Synapse: +5.0 element accuracy, +4.0 step success rate.
limits: Different base prompts and model variants across the systems compared.
agent_relevance: Abstract the case: strip names and values before storing.

source: Zheng et al. (2024) Synapse: Trajectory-as-Exemplar Prompting with Memory for Computer Control (ICLR)
finding: Case = task metadata key plus a whole trajectory (task, observation, action, observation, action). State abstraction trims raw states first. Memory is a vector store keyed on task metadata.
numbers: MiniWoB++ mean success 99.2%, reported as human level and above RCI and AdaPlanner. Mind2Web ablation adds state abstraction, trajectory prompting, then memory step by step on CodeLlama-7B and GPT-3.5.
limits: MiniWoB++ is a simplified suite. Exact Mind2Web numbers are in Table 1 (not extracted).
agent_relevance: Store a clean (compressed) state view in the case, not the raw page.

source: Ouyang et al. (2025) ReasoningBank: Scaling Agent Self-Evolving with Reasoning Memory
finding: Memory item = title, description, content (a strategy), distilled from both successful and failed trajectories judged by an LLM. It drops raw action traces. Failures give pitfalls and guardrails.
numbers: WebArena overall success (Gemini-2.5-flash, 684 tasks): no memory 40.5, Synapse 42.1, AWM 44.1, ReasoningBank 48.8, with MaTTS 51.8. Steps fall from 9.7 to 8.3. Gains +8.3, +7.2, +4.6 over no-memory across three backbones.
limits: Success labels come from an LLM judge. Authors tested verifier accuracy down to 50%: stable in the 70% to 90% range, best at 100%.
agent_relevance: Closest to our S9 line: title, when-to-use, content. Include failures.

source: Ouyang et al. (2025) ReasoningBank: Scaling Agent Self-Evolving with Reasoning Memory
finding: Success-only memory does not gain from adding failures; strategy-level memory does. AWM even got worse with failures added.
numbers: WebArena-Shopping, Gemini-2.5-flash: Synapse 40.6 (success only) to 41.7 (with failures). AWM 44.4 to 42.2. ReasoningBank 46.5 to 49.7.
limits: One subset (187 tasks) and one backbone for this comparison.
agent_relevance: Failure lessons need an abstraction step; raw failed traces can mislead.

source: Ouyang et al. (2025) ReasoningBank: Scaling Agent Self-Evolving with Reasoning Memory
finding: Memory-aware test-time scaling: more trials per task give contrastive material for better memory items. Memory makes scaling pay off; scaling without memory is noisy.
numbers: Shopping subset: parallel scaling 49.7 (k=1) to 55.1 (k=5); sequential 49.7 to 54.5. Without memory: parallel 39.0 to 42.2, sequential 37.4 to 40.6, not monotone. SWE-Bench-Verified resolve rate: none 34.2, Synapse 35.4, ReasoningBank 38.8.
limits: Single-run numbers, no confidence intervals. AWM degrades on the Multi (cross-site) subset: 10.3 to 3.4.
agent_relevance: Compare several attempts on one task to write the lesson, then store it.

source: Zhou et al. (2025) Memento: Fine-tuning LLM Agents without Fine-tuning LLMs
finding: Case = (state/task, action/plan, reward/success flag). Only the state is embedded; action and reward kept as raw text. Both successful and failed cases are retrieved. A learned Q-function can rank cases by chance of success.
numbers: GAIA validation 87.88% (GPT-4.1 planner, o3 executor), test 79.40% from memory built on validation. Learning iterations on DeepResearcher: non-parametric 79.84 to 84.85, parametric 80.46 to 85.44 over five iterations.
limits: Test-set memory is built from validation runs; frontier models; no ablation against matched compute. Without CBR the curve is lower but full numbers are in Table 4.
agent_relevance: Reward is a field in the case. Retrieval can learn to prefer cases that led to success.

source: Zhou et al. (2025) Memento: Fine-tuning LLM Agents without Fine-tuning LLMs
finding: Number of retrieved cases K saturates early. K=4 was about best; K=32 gave no gain.
limits: Single planner/executor pair (gpt-4.1 + o4-mini).
agent_relevance: Keep retrieved cases to about 4. Matches DS-Agent direction.

source: Zhou et al. (2025) Memento: Fine-tuning LLM Agents without Fine-tuning LLMs
finding: Case memory helps most on out-of-distribution questions, but effect size depends on task. Planning without memory gave a larger gain than memory on some sets.
numbers: Component ablation: tools alone changed DeepResearcher by -18.0 F1 / -2.1 PM; adding planning (no CBR) +29.1 F1 / +11.5 PM. HLE 24.4 PM.
limits: Memory adds on top of planning; the memory-only effect is modest in the table text.
agent_relevance: Do not assume memory is the main driver; a plan step may do more.

source: Xiong et al. (2025) How Memory Management Impacts LLM Agents: An Empirical Study of Experience-Following Behavior
finding: Experience-following: when a retrieved record's input is similar to the task, the agent copies its output. So bad stored cases spread. Two harms: error propagation and misaligned replay (a correct-looking run that teaches the wrong thing).
numbers: Input-output similarity correlation near Pearson r about 1 at high input similarity (RegAgent). Add-all and coarse-judge additions gave flat or falling success; a strict (human) evaluator kept improving over time.
limits: Four agents (EHRAgent, AgentDriver, CIC-IoT agent, RegAgent). Fixed small memory sometimes beat noisy growing memory.
agent_relevance: Gate what enters S9. A weak judge makes memory worse than none.

source: Xiong et al. (2025) How Memory Management Impacts LLM Agents: An Empirical Study of Experience-Following Behavior
finding: Utility-based deletion: remove a record if the tasks that retrieved it later did badly. Future task outcomes act as free quality labels for the stored case. Needs a reliable evaluator.
numbers: Tested periodic, history-based and combined deletion with strict and coarse addition; periodic deletion cut memory with small loss; history-based gave gains when the evaluator was reliable (Table 2, numbers not extracted). Fine-tuned judge on only 300 trajectories already beat other coarse judges.
limits: History-based deletion variable when the evaluator is noisy.
agent_relevance: Track a hit/win count per case and prune low-utility ones.

source: Sarukkai et al. (2025) Self-Generated In-Context Examples Improve LLM Agents for Sequential Decision-Making Tasks
finding: Storing only successful self-generated trajectories as examples already lifts results. Curating the database (population-based) and individual examples (by retrieval-weighted success value) lift more.
numbers: Naive accumulation: ALFWorld 73% to 89%, Wordcraft 55% to 64%, InterCode-SQL 75% to 79% (gpt-4o-mini). With curation ALFWorld 93%. The gain beat swapping gpt-4o-mini for gpt-4o and matched allowing two to three attempts.
limits: Result varies a lot across five runs of the same procedure (InterCode-SQL, Figure 1). Gains slow after the first 25% of added tasks.
agent_relevance: Early cases have large influence; curate. Gains are fast then flatten.

source: Yang et al. (2024) Buffer of Thoughts (NeurIPS)
finding: Stores abstract thought-templates, not solved instances. A problem distiller extracts variables and constraints, then a template is retrieved by embedding match and instantiated. New templates are added only if not too similar to existing ones.
numbers: Reported gains over prior methods: +11% Game of 24, +20% Geometric Shapes, +51% Checkmate-in-One. Cost about 12% of multi-query methods. Llama3-8B with BoT may beat Llama3-70B.
limits: Gains are the authors' own and largest on tasks with a fixed solution pattern.
agent_relevance: Case-as-template. Dedup on write.

source: Zhang et al. (2026) TextBFGS: A Case-Based Reasoning Approach to Code Optimization via Error-Operator Retrieval
finding: Case = four parts: pre-edit text, error description, abstract fix rule (operator), post-edit text. Retrieval keys on the error description, not on the problem text.
numbers: HumanEval-Hard with a cross-domain case base: error-keyed retrieval 97.78% vs problem-keyed (REMO) 95.56% pass rate, +2.22%. Cross-domain MBPP Plus: error-keyed 74.36% vs problem-keyed 58.12% (+16.24%), baseline 48.72%.
limits: In-domain, problem-keyed retrieval was slightly better (HumanEval 97.56% vs 96.34%). Small benchmarks (HumanEval-Hard about 45 items by the percentages).
agent_relevance: Index S9 cases by the failure signature as well as the problem class.

source: Zhang et al. (2026) TextBFGS: A Case-Based Reasoning Approach to Code Optimization via Error-Operator Retrieval
finding: Problem-keyed retrieval overfits surface features: it works in-domain but collapses across domains. Operator-style cases transfer. Token cost was lower in cross-domain use.
numbers: Cross-domain MBPP Plus for problem-keyed: 58.12%, a drop of 20.51 points. TextBFGS reports -50.6% tokens on HumanEval vs TextGrad-based methods.
limits: Authors' ablation; no independent replication found.
agent_relevance: Mixed key: problem class for easy reuse, error pattern for transfer.

source: Springdrift (2026) auditable persistent runtime for LLM agents with case-based memory
finding: Production-style CBR record: problem-solution-outcome with a utility score. Utility is Laplace-smoothed (successes+1)/(retrievals+2). Retrieval is a six-signal fusion capped at K=4.
numbers: Weights: inverted index 0.25, embedding 0.40, field score 0.10, recency 0.05, domain 0.10, utility 0.10. Synthetic test (800 cases, 200 queries): hybrid P@4 0.883 vs dense cosine 0.796 on hard queries; CBR without embeddings 0.620.
limits: Synthetic benchmark; ground truth uses keyword overlap, which favours the lexical signal. Utility scoring not evaluated longitudinally. Single system.
agent_relevance: A concrete record format plus a win-rate field for each case.

source: CBR-to-SQL (2026) Rethinking Retrieval-based Text-to-SQL using Case-based Reasoning in the Healthcare Domain
finding: Case = masked question skeleton plus entities plus SQL. Entities are replaced by their schema location so retrieval matches on structure. A second step aligns entities. Removing masking or revision lowered accuracy.
numbers: MIMICSQL execution accuracy 0.894 vs 0.860 for single-step RAG; logical form 0.862 vs 0.825. EHRSQL execution 0.895 vs 0.818; logical form 0.729 vs 0.676. With under 10% of training data the gap on EHRSQL grew to 11.9 and 10.2 points.
limits: A fine-tuned graph method (Chen et al. 2026) scored higher on MIMICSQL execution accuracy (0.942). Domain specific.
agent_relevance: Mask surface detail in the key; keep the structure.

source: Review of Case-Based Reasoning for LLM Agents (2025)
finding: Defines a case as (P, S, O, M): problem features, solution actions, outcome metrics, and metadata such as time, conditions and provenance. Proposes extracting each part then indexing it. A survey, not an experiment.
numbers: Cites DS-Agent 100% / 99%, and says CBR agents give better edge-case handling and user trust. No new measurement.
limits: Position and survey; the claimed benefits on trust and graceful degradation are not backed by new data.
agent_relevance: Gives the field names for our S9 record: problem, solution, outcome, metadata.

source: Watson (2024) A Case-Based Persistent Memory for a Large Language Model (ICCBR workshop)
finding: Position paper: use a CBR case base as persistent memory for an LLM. Notes that the 1990s CBR case bases were small (travel base with 1,100 cases) and argues for very large, multimodal, loosely structured cases.
numbers: Travel case base 1,100 cases; case bases with over a million cases appeared only in the 2010s.
limits: No experiment. Opinion paper.
agent_relevance: Historical frame: cases were small and structured; LLM memory may be large and loose.

source: Feng et al. (2023) Case Repositories: Towards Case-Based Reasoning for AI Alignment
finding: Proposes building a repository of cases (questions plus judgments) from seed cases, expert-defined dimensions, LLM-made variations and public judging. Used as precedent for model behaviour.
numbers: No performance numbers. Process proposal for a workshop.
limits: Not tested on a model.
agent_relevance: Cases can carry judgments, not just solutions.

source: Wang and Feldt (2026) DomAgent: Leveraging Knowledge Graphs and Case-Based Reasoning for Domain-Specific Code Generation
finding: Combines a knowledge graph (top-down concepts) with a retrieved case base (bottom-up examples) for domain code. Small open models gain the most.
numbers: DS-1000 pass@1: DomAgent Qwen2.5-7B 39.2%, LLaMA3.1-8B 40.5%, about +2 to +3 points over the best prior coding agent; GPT-4o vanilla 51.0%. Truck CAN-signal task: Qwen2.5-7B 39.62 to 96.64 pass@1; GPT-4o 71.22 to 98.04.
limits: Truck-software result is on a private task set and partly built with hand-picked cases.
agent_relevance: Cases plus a concept index help weak models more than strong ones.

source: Shinn et al. (2023) Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
finding: Stores a verbal reflection after a failed try in an episodic memory buffer and reuses it on the next try of the same task. This is a within-task lesson, not a cross-task case.
numbers: Abstract: 91% pass@1 on HumanEval vs 80% for GPT-4; +22% on AlfWorld, +20% on HotPotQA, +11% on HumanEval over baselines.
limits: Same-task retries only; later work (ExpeL) found reflections in insight extraction hurt (ExpeL Table 3).
agent_relevance: Within-task lesson line; we need the cross-task version.
